ERROR RECOVERY: the walk STOPS at the first recovery node. Nothing counts symbols-per-file against a floor, so a silently half-analysed document reads as analysed — and the module symbol spans the whole root, so a truncated document still has an identity and every visible count stays plausible. Svelte makes it sharper than html: an unclosed `{#if}` does not clip the damage to the broken line, the parser's ERROR span swallows the REST OF THE FILE, so the tail is valid markup inside the error region. Measured on the real corpus, 2.44% of files carry recovery nodes, and when one does what follows is usually good content — a stopping walk discards the majority of a damaged document. Modelled by dropping every relationship and symbol at or after the FIRST reported error, reading the analyzer's own diagnostic rather than the engine's so the mutated result still looks correctly reported. Caught by svelte/error-recovery, whose `Beta` at L12 and `uses shared` at L12 sit after the error and inside its span.

D12 obligation 1 of 2: the MEMBER-READ carriers are dropped. `bind:`, `class:` and `style:` each read a component member in the template, which is the S1 case, and every one was silent before the ruling — roughly 1,857 corpus occurrences including `bind:value` at 581, the most common attribute interaction in the corpus. Removing them drops the component's primary data-flow surface while the document still looks analysed. Selective on the `carrierDirective` provenance flag rather than on a blanket `uses` filter: a blanket drop is caught by a dozen unrelated fixtures and would prove nothing about D12, and the first version of this mutant used a `metadata.context` marker that only the CALL edges carry, so it SURVIVED. Caught by svelte/directive-carriers.

D12 obligation 2 of 2: the FRAMEWORK-INVOKED carriers are dropped. `use:`, `transition:`, `in:`, `out:` and `animate:` are call sites on exactly the argument that made `on:click` one under D8 — Svelte calls an action on mount and a transition on state change by the same mechanism. Their silence was an internal inconsistency rather than a position, and the mutant restores it. Selective by metadata marker so the `on:` handler edges survive and a failure is attributable to this family rather than to the D8 pass. Caught by svelte/directive-carriers.

D7: rune invocations are dropped. A named function handed to a rune that INVOKES its argument ($effect, $effect.pre, $effect.root, $effect.untracked, $derived.by, $host) is a call site, so a component that runs `fn` on every effect tick must say so in its graph — before the ruling these six forms emitted nothing, because the delegate suppresses the rune and the argument is an ordinary identifier no edge was made for. Selective rather than blanket: a blanket 'drop every calls edge' would be caught by any fixture and would prove nothing about D7. Only edges carrying the rune-pass marker are removed, so the js-delegate call inside `$effect(inlineCall())` and the D8 template-handler call both survive, which is what makes a failure attributable to the ruling rather than to the delegate. Caught by svelte/rune-invocations.

The same hole let a segment containing a SPACE through. Found by the differential oracle on cargo's own Cargo.toml, which is the argument for deriving the rule from the specification ("may this be written bare?") rather than from the characters that appear in the sample you happened to test. Caught by toml/dotted-and-quoted-paths.

ONE FUNCTION OWNS A PATH'S SPELLING: the ancestor lookup deciding which DECLARED table owns a section builds prefixes from RAW segments, while the declared-path table is keyed by the QUOTED spelling, so `target.cfg(unix).dependencies` never matches `target."cfg(unix)".dependencies` and a declared ancestor is reported as implied. The section is then filed under the MODULE. The symbol's NAME stays correct — the emit path does quote — so only the CONTAINMENT is wrong, which is why no symbol assertion could see it and why the fixture pins the edge's SOURCE. On cargo's Cargo.toml, `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies.windows-sys]` was filed under the module rather than the parent declared three lines earlier. Caught by toml/dotted-and-quoted-paths.

TOML-IDENTITY: a symbol's name becomes its LAST SEGMENT instead of its full dotted path, so `[workspace.lints.rust]` is `rust` and `package.name` is `name`. The first manifest anyone writes collides — cargo's own has a key named `name` under `[package]` AND under every `[[bin]]` — so the flattened names are not unique and a `contains` edge naming `name` resolves to two nodes. The full path is what makes a file's names unique without a synthetic suffix on every collision. Caught by toml/identity-and-paths.

TOML-IDENTITY: a quoted key segment is joined like a bare one, so a segment containing a dot loses its quotes. Inside `[t]`, `a.b.c` and `"a.b".c` are DIFFERENT TOML keys — three nested tables versus a table literally named `a.b` — and both assemble to `t.a.b.c`, after which the dedupe invents `t.a.b.c#2` and asserts the document declared one key twice when it declared two distinct ones. That is the unresolvable-identity class arriving through the NAMING SCHEME rather than through a missing edge, and re-quoting is TOML's own disambiguation, not an invented escape. Caught by toml/identity-and-paths, which writes all three spellings side by side.

IDENTITY: the module does not own its name in its own file, so a table may take the file's stem. `doc/book/book.toml` declares `[book]`, and relationships address nodes by NAME, so every `contains` edge naming `book` resolves to two nodes. The module's identity comes from its PATH and is not negotiable. This is html's precedence exactly (its `usedNames` starts `{ [moduleName]: 1 }`), and the rule was found by the CORPUS rather than by a fixture: 2 collisions in 684 cargo files, both `<stem>.toml` containing `[<stem>]`. INLINE-TABLE SCOPING: an inline table's keys become symbols of the file. The ruling is that they are part of ONE value expression — `x = { a = 1 }` makes `x` the symbol — and a manifest with 200 dependencies written as `{ version = "...", features = [...] }` would publish 600+ symbols naming nothing a consumer can navigate to alone. Their names are recorded on the key in `metadata.inlineKeys`, so this mutant loses information as well as adding noise. Caught by toml/arrays-and-values.

Caught by k8s-volume-source-not-a-name's `forbidRelationships` rows for `3`, `420`, `a`, `b/c`, `true` and by the child-key set this transform names; the fixture also pins the six refs that MUST survive, so a fix that stopped emitting resource references outright would fail it.

C0 REVERT, the lane's largest measured defect: symbol identity collapses from `(kind, resolved name)` back to one node per syntactic occurrence, which is what 36.6% of corpus files emitted — the same selector up to 12 times in one file. 27,321 duplicate symbols removed across the wave, 0 remaining in 454 corpus files. Caught by layer-ordering-and-font-families' three `expectSymbolCount` rows, each pinning `equals: 1` for a layer named by BOTH an ordering statement and a block.

C1 REVERT: a `@property` registration publishes `@property --brand` instead of the bare `--brand`, so every `var()` read of a registered property dangles — 273 registrations across 3 corpus files, no read resolving. Caught by font-faces-and-registered-properties, whose `references` row names target `--brand` exactly.

C2 REVERT: `@counter-style`, `@custom-media` and `@font-feature-values` publish no symbol, so every use of one has no endpoint. Zero occurrences in 533 corpus files across 13 repositories, which is why no corpus measurement found it and why the census's NO OCCURRENCE cell read as an all-clear. Caught by declarations-the-corpus-never-uses' three `expectSymbols` rows.

C3 REVERT: the `@layer a, b, c;` ordering form publishes ONE symbol named for the whole statement — `@layer reset, base, components` — a name with no referent that also duplicates the individually declared layers. Caught by layer-ordering-and-font-families' `forbidSymbols` row, which names that exact string.

C4 REVERT: every symbol's complexity is 1, which is the pre-fix emission in full — measured 9,338 of 9,338 symbols at exactly 1. Caught by complexity-matrix, whose rows pin a `:is()` chain above 1 and a scope-conditional block above 1.

C5 REVERT: the `contains` edges from every scoping construct are dropped — `@layer` (7,601), `@media` (2,921), `@container` (11) and `@supports` (1,376, and ZERO before its own fix). The scope symbol and the rules are all still published, so the graph can list both and never their membership. Caught by scope-conditions-and-custom-properties and layer-ordering-and-font-families, which pin `isLayerScope`/`isSupportsScope`/`isMediaScope` rows.

C6 REVERT: the `uses` edges from a `font-family` to a declared `@font-face` are dropped, along with the `list-style` -> `@counter-style` and `font-feature-settings` -> `@font-feature-values` twins. Measured pre-fix: 135 corpus files declare a `font-family`, 21 declare an `@font-face`, 344 family symbols published, and nothing connected them. Caught by layer-ordering-and-font-families' `isFontFamilyRef` row and declarations-the-corpus-never-uses' two `uses` rows.

C7 REVERT: every `var(--x)` read edge is dropped, which is the largest `references` class in the corpus at 13,218 edges, and with it the `@media (--narrow)` -> `--narrow` dependency. Every custom property stays published as a declaration with no reader. Caught by scope-conditions-and-custom-properties' `references` rows.

M59/#855 REVERT: every relationship loses its `line_number`, so 7,662 relationships that each point at a real line become unlocatable. No symbol or edge count changes, which is why this class is invisible to every gate that counts. Caught by M59 oracle-callsite and the CSS line oracle, which compare each edge's line against the source.

REVERT: every relationship loses `metadata.evidenceClass`, so a consumer can no longer tell a STRUCTURAL edge (containment, read from the tree) from a USAGE_CONTEXTUAL one (a `font-family` naming a family) or an IMPORT_BASED one (a `@import` target). The edges are all still there and all still correct, which is what makes the class worth a mutant: the defect is a claim becoming unverifiable rather than a count changing. Caught by the fixtures' `meta.evidenceClass` rows.

REVERT: the `errors` array is emptied, so a stylesheet the grammar could not read is reported as extracted cleanly. Error recovery is why a broken file still yields its surrounding rules, and that is correct — the defect is not the recovery but the COUNT, because every gate that does not read `errors` then sees a successful extraction of a file that failed. This is the class behind the lane's declared 25-file parse floor. Caught by the fixtures' `expectErrorCount` rows.

REVERT: the `isLayerScope`/`isMediaScope`/`isContainerScope`/`isSupportsScope`/`isScopeScope` markers are stripped from relationship metadata, so a consumer must re-parse a scope's NAME to learn what KIND of scope it is. Caught by the fixtures' `meta.isLayerScope` and `meta.isSupportsScope` rows.

REVERT: the markers that say which construct DECLARED a symbol are stripped. `@custom-media` publishes a bare `--narrow`, which is the same shape as a registered `@property` symbol and a rule-level custom property, so without `isCustomMediaDeclaration` / `isPropertyRegistration` / `isCounterStyleDeclaration` the three are indistinguishable in the graph. Two fields holding one value, or three fields holding none, is the same 'two truths' defect the complexity metric carried. Caught by declarations-the-corpus-never-uses' three marker rows and font-faces-and-registered-properties' `isPropertyRegistration` row.

S10 REVERT: two control-flow scopes with identical text collapse back into one symbol, so the second publishes nothing and the owner of everything inside it disappears. Identity by (kind, name) is CORRECT for a $variable — one thing assigned in several places — and wrong for a scope. Measured: two each_statements (L76, L266) in checkbox.scss, and 7 MISSING differential rows that were the analyzer losing information rather than the truth being wrong. Caught by identically-named-scopes-are-distinct, which pins BOTH the plain name and the #2 disambiguation.

S0 REVERT: a `$variable` is published once per ASSIGNMENT rather than once per name, so `$brand` assigned twice is two indistinguishable symbols and a `references` edge addresses one of them. The occurrence count is read from the SOURCE, because a result-derived count is always 1 after the fix and the transform would be a no-op — the exact bug the CSS lane's first identity mutant had, where it SURVIVED. Caught by variables-flags-and-identity's `expectSymbolCount` rows, which pin `$brand` and `$pad` at exactly 1 while the source assigns `$brand` twice.

S1 REVERT: `scssFlagDefault` and `scssFlagGlobal` stop being recorded, so a `!default` assignment is indistinguishable from an ordinary one. This is the first implementation's actual behaviour, for two stacked reasons: the walk used `namedChild` and the flag is two ANONYMOUS nodes, and the test looked for `!default` inside one node's text when the `!` and the word are separate nodes. 210 occurrences in the corpus. Caught by variables-flags-and-identity's two `meta.scssFlag*` rows.

S2 REVERT: an `@use '<mod>' as <ns>` namespace stops being published, so `map.merge(…)` has no endpoint and the binding the statement creates is invisible. This is the first implementation's actual behaviour, which excluded `sass:` modules as 'not the file's own' — a rule nobody wrote down. Caught by module-system-and-mixins' `{ name: 'map', kind: 'namespace' }` row.

S3 REVERT, and it ADDS rather than removes: `@return` emits `contains` from a function to ITSELF. A self-edge makes a relationship count look like evidence while connecting nothing, and it is syntactically well-formed — two real endpoints, nothing malformed — so it is the class a mutant suite catches better than a reading. This is what the first implementation did. Caught by functions-return-and-undeclared-uses' forbidRelationships row.

S4 REVERT: an `@include` of a mixin the file does not declare gets a `uses` edge to a name nothing publishes — the `global` phantom the CSS lane removed once, which a mixin from another stylesheet would bring straight back. Caught by functions-return-and-undeclared-uses' forbidRelationships row naming `not-declared-here`. The negative half is the half that distinguishes a lane from a faucet.

S5 REVERT: when no published symbol contains a statement, the edge is named after its own TARGET rather than skipped. That is the pre-fix behaviour and it produced three fabrications in one file — `uses button -> @mixin button`, `uses .btn -> .btn`, and a source that was raw declaration text. Ownership is now resolved by RANGE. Caught by control-flow-and-extend's `uses .card -> .btn` row, which the fallback turns into `.btn -> .btn` and trips the fixture's own forbidRelationship.

S6 REVERT: a `@mixin`/`@function` symbol loses its `parameters`, so a mixin's signature — the thing a call site is checked against — is absent while the symbol still looks whole. Caught by module-system-and-mixins' and functions-return-and-undeclared-uses' `expectParameters` rows.

S7 REVERT: `@extend` emits no edge, so a rule's inheritance by selector extension is invisible while both selectors still appear as symbols — the graph can list them and never their relation. Caught by control-flow-and-extend's `meta.isScssExtend` row.

S8 REVERT: `@use`/`@forward` stop producing imports, so a stylesheet's entire dependency on the Sass module system disappears from the result while its symbols all remain. Caught by module-system-and-mixins' `expectImports` rows, which pin both the module and the `as` namespace.

S9 REVERT: a control-flow scope stops recording its `@each` key/value, `@for` from/through and `@if` condition, so the scope symbol still looks whole while the only statement of intent the construct makes is gone. Caught by control-flow-and-extend's `meta.scssEachKey`/`scssEachValue`/`scssForFrom`/`scssForThrough` rows.

M59/#855 REVERT: every relationship loses its `line_number`. No symbol or edge COUNT changes, which is why this class is invisible to every gate that counts. Caught by M59 oracle-callsite and the SCSS line oracle.

REVERT: every relationship loses `metadata.evidenceClass`, so a consumer cannot tell a STRUCTURAL edge (`@extend`, containment) from a USAGE_CONTEXTUAL one (`@include`, a `$var` read) or an IMPORT_BASED one (`@use`). All the edges are still there and all still correct, which is what makes the class worth a mutant: the defect is a claim becoming unverifiable rather than a count changing. Caught by the fixtures' `meta.evidenceClass` rows.

REVERT: the `errors` array is emptied, so a stylesheet the grammar could not read is reported as extracted cleanly. This class is the reason the CSS lane needed an `error-recovery-is-reported` fixture at all: every CSS fixture originally asserted `expectErrorCount: 0`, which an EMPTY array satisfies, so the suite could not tell a clean parse from a swallowed failure. Caught by error-recovery-is-reported's `atLeast: 1`.

REVERT: the markers that say which SCSS construct DECLARED a symbol are stripped, so a `$variable` is indistinguishable from a registered `@property` and a control-flow `interface` from a `@supports` one. Caught by variables-flags-and-identity's `meta.isScssVariable` and control-flow-and-extend's `meta.isScssControlFlow` rows.

REVERT: every `uses` edge to a `@function` CALLED in a value disappears, so a declared function can never be reached from its call site and the graph cannot answer "who calls double". Found by the M12 independent hand audit of validation/m12/fixtures/scss/Theme.scss — 9 facts expected, 8 observed, recall 0.889, and the single false negative was this edge. It survived because a `@var` read on the line above was caught and a call on the line below was not: the two are the same class of claim and only one of them was implemented, so no count-based gate could see the gap.

REVERT: `metadata.scssRecoveredFromError` is stripped, so a claim the analyzer only recovered from inside a broken region becomes indistinguishable from one it read cleanly. The EDGES all survive this mutant, so every count-based gate passes; what is lost is the ability to tell a consumer which claims rest on a region the grammar could not read. The control for it is the same variable read twice in one fixture, once recovered and once clean.

REVERT: `metadata.isScssFunctionCall` is stripped, so a call to a user function is indistinguishable from an `@include` of a mixin — both are `uses`. A consumer could no longer tell a value-position call from a statement-position include, which is the difference between "this function is called" and "this block is included".

MD-2 REVERT: a repeated site is collapsed back to its first occurrence, i.e. the `owner + name` key that erased 1,920 of the grammar's 4,078 `fenced_code_block` nodes across 406 of 738 corpus files (worst case docs/_spec/05-classes-and-objects.md, 79 sites published as 24 symbols). Caught by markdown/code-block-site-identity, whose `expectSymbolCount { equals: 2 }` on a two-block owner cannot be satisfied by a name-keyed lane.

MD-1 REVERT: no edge is published for a reference link, i.e. the state in which 671 sites (44 uses + 627 definitions) across 66 of 738 corpus files produced nothing while the lane doc claimed 'Links (inline and reference destinations)'. Caught by markdown/reference-links and F9-PROBE-MD1.

MD-D1 REVERT: an UNDEFINED reference link publishes a `uses` edge to its bare label. Measured on the corpus before it was rejected: 171 edges over 34 files, dominated by bare bracketed citation markers (`NOTICE.md: document -> 1`, six times in one file) — fabricated endpoints and an R10 target-spelling violation. Caught by markdown/reference-links' `forbidRelationships` and F9-PROBE-MD1b, whose forbidden half is asserted on the ORACLE too, so a lane that agreed with itself about this would fail as collusion.

M59 REVERT: no relationship carries `line_number`, i.e. the state in which 0 of 9,132 relationships had one while 35 of 41 sibling analyzers published it. Three measured consequences: bb_graph's line-guarded caller/callee dedup skips every markdown edge, bb_doc renders markdown citations with no `#L` anchor (85% NULL, the worst language in the index), and the store's `(source, type, target, line)` key cannot separate two sites of one target — which is what made the code-block identity defect unrecoverable. Caught by markdown/payload-lines-evidence, whose `_everyRelationshipCarries` names all seven lines.

M14 #419-D REVERT: no edge carries `evidenceClass`. The lane's own edges are then judged by graph-core's read-time derivation, whose STRUCTURAL_TYPES set does not contain `contains` — so the entire heading hierarchy, a direct AST parent/child relation, was rendered to readers as `inferred`: 'a guess, treat as a hint, never as fact'. Measured before the fix: 0 of 9,132 relationships carried a class. Caught by markdown/payload-lines-evidence's two `meta.evidenceClass` assertions.

REVERT: `isRepeatedSite` is no longer set on a repeat. The repeats themselves still publish (so this is subtler than the identity collapse), but a consumer can no longer tell one code block from the next. Caught by markdown/code-block-site-identity's third `expectSymbols` entry.

MD-6 REVERT: an ATX heading's closing `#` run stays in its published name, so `# H #` publishes `H #`. A document that closes its headings and one that does not then produce two different symbols for the same section. Caught by markdown/heading-identity's `forbidSymbols { "Closed with a trailing run ##" }` and F9-PROBE-MD10.

MD-8 REVERT: an empty ATX heading publishes a symbol named after its OWN MARKER, so a document of empty headings produces a `contains` chain named `#` -> `##` -> `###`. That is the M60 R7 class — a name that is not a name, one step short of the register's own MARKER pattern — and two sibling `##` headings both named `##` collided, so every heading after them was attributed to the empty `#` as its owner. Caught by markdown/heading-identity's `forbidSymbols` and F9-PROBE-MD9.

MD-7 REVERT: a multi-line setext heading's name is every line but the underline, so it carries an embedded NEWLINE into `ownerName`, the qualified path and every display surface. Measured pre-fix: "Multi Line Title\nsecond line of paragraph". Caught by markdown/heading-identity, whose `expectSymbolCount { equals: 1 }` on the setext name fails when the name carries the continuation line.

The only ADDITIVE mutant here, and the most valuable: a link inside a `code_span` or a closed fence is published as a link. Every other mutant removes a fact; this one adds one, by descending into children the named-child walk structurally cannot reach — the inline grammar gives a `code_span` only ANONYMOUS children, so a `link_destination` is unreachable beneath one and the exclusion is a property a reader can check rather than a filter someone remembered. If this mutant SURVIVES, the analyzer is right and the pin is wrong, which is the only direction a subtraction-only mutant set can never reveal. Caught by markdown/reference-links' `forbidRelationships` and F9-PROBE-MD6.

REVERT: a repeated site publishes the BARE name again while its edge keeps the suffixed spelling, i.e. the state this round measured at 529 of 1,843 relationships (28.7%) over 120 scala3 markdown files naming a symbol the file did not declare. The store keys a relationship by (source, type, target, line) and checks the target name against a denylist rather than for existence, so an unsatisfiable name does not fail loudly -- it writes a row referencing a symbol id no symbol row has. The diff could not see it: the independent oracle derives the same suffixed spelling, so both sides agreed on a name neither published, and two implementations sharing a convention is not evidence that the convention resolves. Caught by markdown/code-block-site-identity's `expectSymbolCount { name: code_block.scala#2, equals: 1 }` and by markdown/table-structure's `forbidSymbols { Name/Meaning#2 }`.

REVERT: the heading-hierarchy edge is dropped whenever the two ends spell the same string, i.e. the self-edge filter is asked about NAMES rather than about identity. A `## Changelog` under a `# Changelog` is two distinct sites -- the child's id is qualified by its parent's -- so the containment is real and the edge must be published. Found by the differential rather than by the read, and found quietly: the tree oracle derives the edge from the grammar, the analyzer did not have it, and the kubernetes draw read MISSING=1 in about one draw in nine (`vendor/github.com/google/uuid/CHANGELOG.md`), which is the rate at which a reader writes a count off as sampling noise. Caught by markdown/heading-parent-name-collision, whose two `Changelog -> Changelog` rows and `Setup -> Setup` row cannot be satisfied by a name-keyed filter.

REVERT: a table column declares no symbol, while its `table_column` edge is still emitted -- the state in which the analyzer's own comment said 'a column is a site too' and the site never shipped. Measured after the repeat-site fix, over the same 120 files, 31 endpoints still named no symbol and every remaining one was a column. The edges survive this mutant on purpose: that is what made the defect invisible, because a count of relationships cannot tell an edge to nothing from an edge to something. Caught by markdown/table-structure's `isMarkdownTableColumn` assertions and its `Reading -> Reading` column edge.

REVERT: a same-document reference is published with its RAW FRAGMENT as the target, i.e. the state this round measured at 10,174 fragments in a 420-file draw, every one an edge to a name no symbol declared. A link writes a heading's ANCHOR and the lane published heading TEXT, so the two spellings could not meet: `## Install Now!` publishes as `Install Now!` and a link to it says `#install-now`, and nothing in the file is called `install-now`. 10,158 of those references now resolve and 16 name a heading that does not exist. The differential could not see it for the same reason it could not see MD-12: the oracle derived the same raw fragment, so the two agreed at 100% on a name neither published. Caught by markdown/internal-anchor-links' `forbidRelationships`, whose rows name the raw fragment specifically because an implementation that resolved nothing and one that resolved everything-but-wrote-the-fragment both look correct to a count.

MD-G1 REVERT: an INDENTED (four-space) code block publishes nothing, while the fenced form beside it publishes a per-site `function`. Measured with the block grammar over 1,138 pinned corpus files: 217 `indented_code_block` nodes, every one of them a node the grammar names. The gap originally recorded 2 sites, measured by a text heuristic; the grammar is 100x that, and most of the 217 are the wrapped continuation lines of deeply-nested list items, which CommonMark genuinely reads as indented code. So the revert deletes 217 symbols, which is why the symbol COUNT is the assertion here and not a name: a lane that published them under a different name would satisfy a name filter and still lose the construct. Caught by markdown/indented-code-block, whose expectSymbolCount totals 6 blocks across 3 sections and whose `Not a code block` forbid rows stop the fixture being satisfied by treating any indented line as code.
